note: Spoken to a governor rebuilding a temple with no army and no treasury — the promise is specifically about small beginnings, not a general slogan.

title: How does Zechariah portray the shepherd struck?
answer: 'Smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.'
note: Jesus applies it to himself and the disciples on the night of his arrest (Matt 26:31), reading his abandonment as scripted rather than accidental.

title: What does Malachi say about the messenger before the Lord?
answer: That he will prepare the way, and the Lord shall suddenly come to his temple.
note: Mark opens his Gospel by fusing this with Isaiah 40, identifying John the Baptist as the messenger and Jesus as the Lord who comes.

title: Which three Gospels are called Synoptic, and why?
answer: Matthew, Mark and Luke — they "see together," sharing much common material and order.
note: Synoptic means 'seen together'; their extensive verbal agreement raises the Synoptic Problem, and Markan priority with a shared sayings source is the majority scholarly solution.

title: To whom is each Gospel especially addressed?
answer: Matthew to Jews (Christ the King), Mark to Romans (the Servant), Luke to Greeks (the Son of Man), John to all (the Son of God).

title: What is the stated purpose of John's Gospel?
answer: That you may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and believing have life in his name.
note: John 20:31 states the aim as belief leading to life, and the Greek tense is disputed between 'come to believe' and 'continue believing' — evangelistic or pastoral intent turns on it.

title: How does John's Gospel open?
answer: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."

title: What does John 1:14 declare about the Word?
answer: "The Word became flesh, and dwelt among us" — the doctrine of the Incarnation.
note: 'Full of grace and truth' renders the Hebrew pair chesed and emet from Exodus 34:6, so John presents Jesus as the personal embodiment of the covenant name revealed to Moses.

title: How many women are named in Matthew's genealogy, and who?
answer: Four before Mary: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and "her that had been the wife of Uriah."

title: What did the angel say Jesus' name would mean?
answer: "He shall save his people from their sins."
note: Yeshua means 'the LORD saves,' and Matthew 1:21's 'he shall save his people from their sins' quietly assigns to Jesus a work Scripture reserves to God.

title: What does "Immanuel" mean?
answer: "God with us."

title: What is Mary's song called, and what does it celebrate?
answer: The Magnificat — God exalting the humble and scattering the proud.
note: The Magnificat's verbs are past tense — God 'hath put down' and 'hath exalted' — treating the reversal as already accomplished in the conception, before anything visible has changed.

title: What two songs frame Luke's nativity besides the Magnificat?
answer: Zacharias' Benedictus and Simeon's Nunc Dimittis.

title: What sign was given to the shepherds?
answer: A babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.
note: The sign is a baby in a feeding trough: the least impressive confirmation imaginable, given to the least reputable audience, which is Luke's argument in miniature.

title: What three gifts did the wise men bring, and what has tradition read into them?
answer: Gold (kingship), frankincense (deity/priesthood), myrrh (burial and suffering).

title: What is the only recorded event of Jesus' boyhood?
answer: At twelve, in the temple among the teachers: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

title: What did John the Baptist preach, and what did he call Jesus?
answer: Repentance for the kingdom of heaven is at hand; "Behold, the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world."
note: 'Lamb of God' fuses the Passover lamb, the daily sacrifice and Isaiah 53's silent lamb into one title before Jesus has performed a single act of ministry.

title: What happened at Jesus' baptism?
answer: The Spirit descended as a dove and the Father spoke — one of Scripture's clearest Trinitarian scenes.
note: All three Persons are manifest at once — Son in the water, Spirit descending, Father speaking — making it the clearest trinitarian scene in the Gospels.

title: How did Jesus answer each of the three temptations?
answer: With Scripture — "It is written" — each time quoting Deuteronomy.
note: Every answer comes from Deuteronomy 6-8, the passage about Israel's wilderness testing; where Israel failed over forty years, Jesus succeeds over forty days.

title: What are the Beatitudes?
answer: The eight (or nine) blessings opening the Sermon on the Mount, describing the character of kingdom citizens.
note: They are declarations rather than commands — 'blessed are,' not 'be blessed' — describing the condition of those already in the kingdom rather than entry requirements.

title: What two images did Jesus give his disciples in the Sermon on the Mount?
answer: Salt of the earth and light of the world.

title: What is the Golden Rule?
answer: "All things therefore whatsoever ye would that men should do unto you, even so do ye also unto them."
note: Its positive form distinguishes it from the negative version found in Hillel and Confucius; refraining from harm is not the same as taking initiative in good.

title: What did Jesus say he came to do with the Law?
answer: Not to destroy but to fulfil it.
note: 'Not to destroy, but to fulfil' governs everything that follows in Matthew 5, where the antitheses intensify rather than relax the commandments.

title: How many petitions are in the Lord's Prayer?
answer: Six (or seven, depending on division) — three concerning God's name, kingdom and will, then bread, forgiveness, and deliverance.
note: Six or seven depending on how the final clause is counted, and the first three concern God's name, kingdom and will — the ordering is itself the lesson.

title: What was Jesus' first recorded miracle, and where?
answer: Turning water into wine at the wedding in Cana of Galilee.
note: John calls it the 'beginning of signs' and notes it manifested his glory; the setting at a wedding and the abundance of the wine both anticipate the messianic banquet.

title: How many named "signs" structure John's Gospel?
answer: Seven, from Cana to the raising of Lazarus.

title: List the seven "I AM" sayings of John's Gospel.
answer: Bread of life; light of the world; the door; the good shepherd; the resurrection and the life; the way, the truth, and the life; the true vine.
note: Each echoes the divine name of Exodus 3:14 — John 8:58 makes the claim explicit.

title: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus was necessary to see the kingdom?
answer: To be born again — born of water and of the Spirit.
note: The Greek 'anothen' means both 'again' and 'from above,' and Nicodemus hears only the first — the misunderstanding is built into the word.

title: Which verse is often called the gospel in miniature?
answer: John 3:16 — "God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son."
note: John 3:16's 'gave' points forward to the cross rather than to the incarnation alone, and the verb for 'loved' is in the aorist, pointing to a decisive historical act.

title: What did Jesus tell the Samaritan woman God seeks?
answer: Worshippers who worship in spirit and in truth.

title: How many disciples did Jesus choose, and why that number?
answer: Twelve, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel — a new covenant people.
note: Twelve corresponds to the tribes, so the choice is a claim: Jesus is constituting a renewed Israel around himself, which is why replacing Judas mattered in Acts 1.

title: What is the shortest verse in the Bible, and where?
answer: "Jesus wept," at the tomb of Lazarus.
note: 'Jesus wept' occurs when he already knows he will raise Lazarus — grief is not rendered inappropriate by the certainty of resurrection.

title: What are the parables of Luke 15?
answer: The lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost (prodigal) son — three pictures of God's joy over one sinner repenting.
note: All three answer the complaint of verse 2 that 'this man receiveth sinners.' The third parable ends without resolving whether the elder brother comes in — the Pharisees are left to finish the story.

title: What question prompted the parable of the Good Samaritan?
answer: "And who is my neighbour?"

title: What did Jesus tell Martha was needful?
answer: One thing — the good part Mary had chosen, sitting at his feet.

title: What confession did Peter make at Caesarea Philippi?
answer: "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God."
note: The location matters: Caesarea Philippi was a centre of pagan worship at the Gates of Hades, which gives Jesus' reply about the gates of hell its local force.

title: What new commandment did Jesus give in the upper room?
answer: "That ye love one another; even as I have loved you."
note: Its newness lies in the standard — 'as I have loved you' — not in the command to love, which is already in Leviticus 19:18.

title: What act of service did Jesus perform at the Last Supper?
answer: He washed the disciples' feet.

title: Who is the Comforter Jesus promised?
answer: The Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth, sent from the Father.
note: 'Parakletos' means one called alongside, and the term is legal as much as consolatory; 1 John 2:1 uses the same word of Christ, making the Spirit 'another' advocate of the same kind.

title: What did Jesus pray three times in Gethsemane?
answer: That the cup might pass — "nevertheless, not as I will, but as thou wilt."

title: What are the seven sayings of Christ from the cross?
answer: Forgiveness for his killers; paradise to the thief; care of his mother; the cry of dereliction; "I thirst"; "It is finished"; and commending his spirit.
note: They move from intercession for others, through provision for his mother, to abandonment, thirst, completion and commitment — a sequence the Church has meditated on liturgically since the Middle Ages.

title: What happened to the temple veil at Jesus' death?
answer: It was rent in two from the top to the bottom.
note: Top-down: access to God opened by God's act, not man's.

title: Who first saw the risen Christ?
answer: Mary Magdalene, at the tomb.
note: Mary Magdalene, who mistook him for the gardener — an irony readers have long noted, given that the first Adam's failure took place in a garden.

title: What did Thomas say when he saw the risen Christ?
answer: "My Lord and my God" — the Gospel's climactic confession of Christ's deity.

title: What is the Great Commission?
answer: To go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching, with the promise of Christ's presence to the end of the age.

title: Who was the aged man told he would not die before seeing the Christ?
answer: Simeon, who then sang the Nunc Dimittis.

title: Which aged prophetess spoke of the child in the temple?
answer: Anna, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser.

title: Why did the holy family flee to Egypt?
answer: Herod sought the young child's life; it fulfilled 'Out of Egypt have I called my son.'

title: What was John the Baptist's clothing and food?
answer: Camel's hair with a leathern girdle; locusts and wild honey.

title: What did John say must happen to him and to Christ?
answer: 'He must increase, but I must decrease.'

title: Who were the first disciples called by the sea?
answer: Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John.

title: What did Jesus say about salt that loses savour?
answer: It is good for nothing but to be cast out and trodden under foot.

title: What did Jesus teach about giving alms?
answer: Do not sound a trumpet; let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth.

title: What are the two masters of Matthew 6?
answer: God and mammon — no man can serve both.

title: What should be sought first?
answer: 'Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.'

title: What two builders close the Sermon on the Mount?
answer: The wise man on rock and the foolish man on sand.

title: Whose faith did Jesus say he had not found in Israel?
answer: The centurion's, who said 'speak the word only.'

title: How did Jesus still the storm, and what did the disciples ask?
answer: He rebuked wind and sea; they asked, 'What manner of man is this?'

title: What did Jesus say about the harvest and labourers?
answer: 'The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.'

title: What invitation does Matthew 11 give the weary?
answer: 'Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.'

title: What sin did Jesus call unforgivable?
answer: Blasphemy against the Holy Ghost.
note: In context it is attributing the Spirit's manifest work to Satan — a settled, knowing repudiation, not a passing doubt.

title: What four soils appear in the parable of the sower?
answer: The wayside, stony places, among thorns, and good ground.

title: What two small parables describe the kingdom's worth?
answer: The treasure hid in a field and the pearl of great price.

title: Who appeared with Jesus at the Transfiguration?
answer: Moses and Elias, talking with him.
note: Law and Prophets attend the Son, and the voice says 'hear ye him' — the two witnesses yield to the one Word.

title: How often did Jesus say to forgive?
answer: 'Until seventy times seven.'

title: Where is Christ present among two or three?
answer: 'There am I in the midst of them,' gathered in his name.

title: What did the rich young ruler lack?
answer: One thing — to sell what he had, give to the poor, and follow Christ.

title: What did Jesus say about the camel and the needle's eye?
answer: It is easier than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God — but with God all things are possible.

title: What are the two great commandments?
answer: Love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, soul and mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.

title: What did Jesus call the weightier matters of the law?
answer: Judgment, mercy, and faith.

title: What sign did Jesus give of the end of the age in Matthew 24?
answer: The gospel of the kingdom preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations.

title: What three parables of readiness fill Matthew 25?
answer: The ten virgins, the talents, and the sheep and the goats.

title: What did the King say the righteous had done to him?
answer: 'Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.'

title: What did Jesus say the Son of man came to give?
answer: 'His life a ransom for many.'

title: What did the poor widow cast into the treasury?
answer: Two mites — all her living, which Jesus said exceeded all the rest.

title: What miraculous catch preceded Peter's call in Luke?
answer: A net-breaking draught after launching into the deep, at which Peter said, 'Depart from me.'

title: Which woman anointed Jesus' feet and was told her sins were forgiven?
answer: A woman of the city who was a sinner, in the house of Simon the Pharisee.

title: What did Jesus tell the seventy to rejoice in?
answer: Not that spirits were subject to them, but that their names were written in heaven.

title: What did the rich fool forget?
answer: That his soul would be required of him that night.

title: What did the prodigal's father do while he was yet a great way off?
answer: He had compassion, ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.

title: What did the publican pray in the temple?
answer: 'God be merciful to me a sinner' — and he went down justified rather than the Pharisee.
note: The Greek is 'be propitiated toward me' — the tax collector asks for exactly what the mercy seat provided.

title: What did Jesus say the Son of man came to do in Luke 19:10?
answer: 'To seek and to save that which was lost.'

title: What did Jesus say to the penitent thief?
answer: 'To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.'

title: What happened on the road to Emmaus?
answer: The risen Christ expounded Moses and all the prophets, and was known in breaking of bread.

title: What did John the Baptist say seeing Jesus approach?
answer: 'Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.'

title: What did Jesus say about destroying 'this temple'?
answer: He spoke of the temple of his body, raised in three days.

title: What did Jesus say about worship in spirit and truth?
answer: The Father seeks such to worship him, for God is a Spirit.

title: What did Jesus say makes men free?
answer: 'Ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.'

title: What claim in John 8 made them take up stones?
answer: 'Before Abraham was, I am.'
note: The unqualified 'I am' takes the divine name of Exod 3:14 onto his own lips — hence the stones.

title: What did Jesus say to Martha before raising Lazarus?
answer: 'I am the resurrection, and the life.'

title: What must a corn of wheat do to bring forth fruit?
answer: Fall into the ground and die.

title: By what did Jesus say all men would know his disciples?
answer: 'If ye have love one to another.'

title: What is the vine-and-branches lesson?
answer: 'Without me ye can do nothing' — abiding is the condition of fruit.

title: What did Jesus pray for in John 17?
answer: That his people be one, kept from evil, and sanctified through the truth.

title: What did Jesus answer Pilate about his kingdom?
answer: 'My kingdom is not of this world.'

title: What were Jesus' words of completion on the cross?
answer: 'It is finished' — a single Greek word, tetelestai.
note: Tetelestai was written across paid accounts: the debt is not merely stopped but discharged in full.

title: What threefold question did Jesus ask Peter by the sea?
answer: 'Lovest thou me?' — restoring him with 'Feed my lambs... my sheep.'

title: Why does Matthew structure his Gospel in five discourses?
answer: To present Jesus as the new Moses giving a new Torah.
note: Each block closes with 'when Jesus had ended these sayings' — a deliberate seam marking the fivefold pattern against the Pentateuch.

title: What is unusual about the women in Matthew's genealogy?
answer: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and Bathsheba are all outsiders or associated with scandal.
note: Their inclusion signals from verse one that this Messiah's line runs through Gentiles and moral disorder, not around them.

title: What does Mark's 'messianic secret' refer to?
answer: Jesus repeatedly silencing demons and healed people about his identity.
note: The silence lifts at the cross, where a Roman centurion — not a disciple — makes the Gospel's full confession (Mark 15:39).

title: Who is the first human in Mark to call Jesus the Son of God?
answer: The centurion at the cross, seeing how he died.
note: Mark 1:1 announces it, God declares it at the baptism, demons know it — but the first human confession comes from an executioner at a corpse.

title: What is distinctive about Luke's interest?
answer: The poor, women, Samaritans, tax collectors and outsiders.
note: Luke alone records the Good Samaritan, the prodigal, Zacchaeus and the penitent thief — his selection is itself an argument.

title: What did Mary's Magnificat announce about social order?
answer: That God puts down the mighty and exalts the lowly, filling the hungry and sending the rich empty away.
note: Deliberately modelled on Hannah's song (1 Sam 2), placing the incarnation in a long line of God's reversals.

title: Why does John have no parables and no exorcisms?
answer: His method is extended discourse and sign, presenting Christ's identity directly.
note: John's seven signs each provoke a discourse unpacking their meaning — the miracle is never left to speak alone.

title: What does the prologue of John claim about the Word?
answer: He was in the beginning with God, was God, and all things were made by him.
note: The deliberate echo of Gen 1:1 places Jesus on the Creator's side of the creature line before the Gospel narrates a single event.

title: What does John mean by 'the Word became flesh and dwelt among us'?
answer: That God took a full human nature and pitched his tent among his people.
note: The verb is 'tabernacled,' and the following clause 'we beheld his glory' recalls the glory filling the tabernacle in Exod 40:34.

title: What was the first thing Jesus preached?
answer: 'Repent ye, and believe the gospel: the kingdom of God is at hand.'
note: Repentance and faith are presented as a single response, and the kingdom is announced as arriving rather than merely approaching.

title: How does Jesus define greatness in the kingdom?
answer: By becoming least and servant of all, like a child.
note: He teaches it immediately after the disciples argue about rank — the lesson is delivered as a rebuke, not an abstraction.

title: What is the point of the parable of the labourers in the vineyard?
answer: That God's generosity is not injustice, though it offends those who calculate desert.
note: The complaint 'thou hast made them equal unto us' is the parable's real subject: grace is intolerable to a merit economy.

title: What does the parable of the unforgiving servant teach?
answer: That one forgiven an unpayable debt cannot withhold forgiveness of a trivial one.
note: The ten thousand talents against a hundred pence is a ratio of roughly 600,000 to one — the disproportion is the whole argument.

title: Why did Jesus speak in parables?
answer: So that seeing they might not see — revealing to the receptive and concealing from the hardened.
note: Parables are not simple illustrations but sifting instruments; they demand engagement and reward it, while the indifferent hear only a story.

title: What did Jesus say defiles a person?
answer: Not what enters the mouth but what proceeds out of the heart.
note: Mark adds the editorial 'purging all meats' (7:19), reading the saying as abolishing the food laws — a claim with enormous implications for Acts 10.

title: What did Jesus mean by taking up the cross?
answer: A daily readiness to die to self and follow, using the image of a condemned man's walk.
note: To first-century hearers the cross was not jewellery but an execution instrument; the metaphor was brutal, not devotional.

title: What was the sign of Jonah Jesus offered?
answer: Three days and nights, as Jonah in the fish, so the Son of man in the heart of the earth.
note: The only sign he grants to a demanding generation is his resurrection — the miracle they will refuse to accept.

title: What happened at Caesarea Philippi after Peter's confession?
answer: Jesus began to teach that he must suffer, and rebuked Peter as Satan for resisting it.
note: The confession of Christ is correct but incomplete until it includes the cross; a Messiah without suffering is a satanic proposal.

title: What did Jesus teach about the widow's mite?
answer: That she cast in more than all, giving of her want rather than her abundance.
note: It follows immediately after his denunciation of scribes who devour widows' houses — the two scenes are meant to be read together.

title: What did the triumphal entry signify?
answer: A deliberate enactment of Zechariah 9:9 — a king coming lowly, riding on an ass.
note: Choosing a donkey rather than a warhorse was a public statement about what kind of kingship was arriving.

title: What did Jesus predict about the temple?
answer: That not one stone would be left upon another.
note: Fulfilled in AD 70; the prediction is one reason many scholars debate Gospel dating, since its specificity is either prophecy or hindsight.

title: What is the significance of the Last Supper being a Passover?
answer: Jesus reinterprets the exodus meal around his own body and blood.
note: He gives no explanation of the lamb, because he is standing where the lamb's explanation used to go.

title: What did Jesus say about the cup at the supper?
answer: 'This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.'
note: The direct invocation of Jeremiah 31:31 identifies his death as the inauguration of the promised new covenant.

title: What was Jesus' charge before the Sanhedrin?
answer: Blasphemy, after affirming he was the Christ and would be seen at the right hand of power.
note: He answers by combining Ps 110:1 and Dan 7:13 — claiming both enthronement and the coming Son of man, which is why the high priest tears his clothes.

title: Why did the Jewish leaders bring Jesus to Pilate?
answer: Because they lacked authority to execute, and shifted the charge from blasphemy to sedition.
note: The charge changes from a religious one Rome would ignore to a political one Rome could not — 'we have no king but Caesar' (John 19:15).

title: What did Pilate write on the cross, and in what languages?
answer: 'JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS,' in Hebrew, Greek and Latin.
note: The three languages of the empire proclaim the title unintentionally to the whole world; Pilate refuses to amend it.

title: What did the women find at the tomb?
answer: The stone rolled away, the tomb empty, and angels declaring he is risen.
note: That women are the first witnesses is a strong argument for historicity, since their testimony carried little legal weight in that culture.

title: What did the risen Christ do to prove he was not a spirit?
answer: He showed his hands and feet and ate a piece of broiled fish before them.
note: The wounds persist in the resurrection body — glorification does not erase history, it vindicates it.

title: What commission does John's Gospel record after the resurrection?
answer: 'As my Father hath sent me, even so send I you,' with the breathing of the Spirit.
note: The breathing recalls Gen 2:7 — new creation language for a newly commissioned people.

title: How does John's Gospel end?
answer: By noting that the world could not contain the books if all Jesus did were written.
note: A deliberate closing signal that the Gospels are selective testimony with a stated purpose (John 20:31), not exhaustive biography.

title: Who wrote Acts, and to whom is it addressed?
answer: Luke, addressed to Theophilus — a second volume continuing his Gospel.

title: What is the outline programme of Acts given in chapter 1?
answer: Witness in Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
note: Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria and the uttermost part of the earth supplies the book's actual structure, and Acts ends in Rome without reaching the final clause — the commission outlives the narrative.

title: How long after the resurrection did Jesus ascend?
answer: Forty days, during which he showed himself alive by many proofs.

title: Who replaced Judas among the twelve?
answer: Matthias, chosen by lot from those who had accompanied Jesus from John's baptism onward.

title: What three signs accompanied Pentecost?
answer: A sound as of rushing mighty wind, tongues as of fire, and speaking in other tongues.
note: Wind, fire and tongues each carry Old Testament freight — the breath of Ezekiel 37, the Sinai fire, and the reversal of Babel's scattering.

title: How many were added to the church at Pentecost?
answer: About three thousand souls.

title: What four things did the early church continue steadfastly in?
answer: The apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers.

title: What happened to Ananias and Sapphira, and why?
answer: They died for lying to the Holy Spirit about the price of their land.

title: Why were the first seven deacons appointed?
answer: To serve tables so the apostles could give themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word.

title: Who was the first Christian martyr, and who consented to his death?
answer: Stephen; Saul of Tarsus was consenting and kept the witnesses' garments.
note: Luke names Saul at the stoning and notes the witnesses laid their clothes at his feet — the persecutor is introduced as a bystander before he becomes the protagonist.

title: What did Stephen see as he died?
answer: The heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

title: What happened to Saul on the Damascus road?
answer: A light from heaven and the voice of Jesus: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?"
note: 'Why persecutest thou me?' identifies Christ with his people so completely that attacking the church is attacking him — the seed of Paul's later body theology.

title: Who was the first Gentile convert, and what vision preceded it?
answer: Cornelius the centurion; Peter's vision of the sheet of unclean animals.

title: Where were disciples first called Christians?
answer: At Antioch.
note: The name was probably coined by outsiders at Antioch and appears only three times in the New Testament; believers usually called themselves disciples, saints or those of 'the Way.'

title: What did the Jerusalem Council decide about Gentile believers?
answer: That they need not be circumcised or keep the Law of Moses to be saved.
note: The decisive moment establishing salvation by grace apart from the Law.

title: How did Peter and John heal the lame man at the Beautiful gate?
answer: 'In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.'

title: What did Peter declare about salvation before the council?
answer: 'There is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.'

title: What did the council note about Peter and John?
answer: That they were unlearned and ignorant men, and 'took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.'

title: What advice did Gamaliel give the council?
answer: Leave them alone — if of men it will come to nought, if of God it cannot be overthrown.

title: Whom did Philip baptize on the Gaza road?
answer: The Ethiopian eunuch, reading Isaiah 53.

title: Who tried to buy the gift of the Spirit, and what word came from it?
answer: Simon the sorcerer — hence 'simony.'

title: Who vouched for Saul before the suspicious disciples?
answer: Barnabas, 'the son of consolation.'

title: How did Peter escape Herod's prison?
answer: An angel woke him and the chains fell off; the iron gate opened of its own accord.

title: Who accompanied Paul on the first missionary journey, and who turned back?
answer: Barnabas and John Mark; Mark departed at Perga.

title: What sharp contention parted Paul and Barnabas?
answer: Whether to take John Mark again; Barnabas took Mark, Paul took Silas.

title: Who was Paul's first European convert?
answer: Lydia, a seller of purple of Thyatira, at Philippi.

title: What did the Philippian jailer ask, and what was the answer?
answer: 'What must I do to be saved?' — 'Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.'

title: Why were the Bereans called more noble?
answer: They received the word readily and searched the scriptures daily to test it.
note: Luke commends a church that fact-checks an apostle — apostolic authority and Berean scrutiny are not in conflict.

title: What altar did Paul cite at Athens?
answer: One inscribed 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD.'

title: What did Paul say about God and human boundaries at Mars' hill?
answer: God made of one blood all nations, determining their times and the bounds of their habitation.

title: Who was instructed more perfectly in the way at Ephesus?
answer: Apollos, taught by Aquila and Priscilla.

title: What riot broke out at Ephesus, and over what?
answer: Demetrius the silversmith stirred it over lost trade in shrines of Diana.

title: What unrecorded saying of Jesus does Paul quote at Miletus?
answer: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'

title: What was Paul's answer to those weeping over his going to Jerusalem?
answer: 'I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.'

title: What right did Paul invoke to avoid scourging?
answer: His Roman citizenship, which he held by birth.

title: How did Paul divide the council in Jerusalem?
answer: By raising the resurrection, dividing Pharisees from Sadducees.

title: Before which three rulers did Paul make his defence?
answer: Felix, Festus, and King Agrippa.

title: What did Agrippa say to Paul?
answer: 'Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.'

title: What happened to Paul on Malta?
answer: A viper fastened on his hand and he shook it off unharmed; he then healed Publius' father.

title: How does Acts end?
answer: Paul in Rome two whole years in his own hired house, preaching 'no man forbidding him.'
note: The open ending is deliberate: the gospel has reached the empire's centre and the story is handed to the reader.

title: What are the recurring summary statements in Acts?
answer: Brief notes that the word of God grew and multiplied.
note: These summaries divide Acts into panels, and the subject of the growth is 'the word' rather than 'the church' — Luke's chosen protagonist.

title: How does Acts 2:42 describe the church's life?
answer: Continuing steadfastly in the apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayers.
note: The four marks became the classic template for evaluating church practice: teaching, community, sacrament and prayer.

title: What was the nature of the early church's sharing of goods?
answer: Voluntary and need-driven, not compulsory or systematic.
note: Peter tells Ananias the land was his own and the money at his disposal — the sin was deception, not private ownership.

title: What was the theological content of Peter's Pentecost sermon?
answer: That Jesus, delivered by God's determinate counsel and slain by wicked hands, was raised and made Lord and Christ.
note: Divine sovereignty and human guilt stand in a single sentence without apology — Luke sees no contradiction requiring resolution.

title: What did Stephen's speech argue?
answer: That God was never confined to the temple and Israel had always resisted the Spirit.
note: His survey ends with the charge that they betrayed the Just One — the speech is a covenant lawsuit in the prophetic mould.

title: How does Acts 8 mark a turning point?
answer: Persecution scatters the church, and the scattered go everywhere preaching.
note: The mission advances by disaster; Luke presents the persecution as the mechanism of the Acts 1:8 programme, not an obstacle to it.

title: What was the theological significance of Cornelius' conversion?
answer: God gave the Gentiles the same Spirit without circumcision, settling the question by act before argument.
note: Peter's defence at Jerusalem is essentially 'who was I, that I could withstand God?' — experience of the Spirit functions as evidence.

title: What vision preceded Peter's visit to Cornelius?
answer: A sheet let down with unclean animals, and the voice 'What God hath cleansed, call not thou common.'
note: The vision is about food but the meaning is about people — Peter says so explicitly in verse 28.

title: How was the Antioch church distinctive?
answer: It was the first substantially Gentile church, and the first to send out missionaries.
note: Its leadership list includes an African and a member of Herod's court — the mission base is deliberately multi-ethnic.

title: What was the Jerusalem Council's theological conclusion?
answer: That Gentiles are saved by grace through faith, as Jews are, without the yoke of the law.
note: Peter's phrasing is striking: not that Gentiles are saved like Jews, but that Jews 'shall be saved, even as they' — the Gentile experience is made the norm.

title: What four abstentions did the Council request?
answer: From things offered to idols, blood, things strangled, and fornication.
note: Widely read as concessions for table fellowship with Jewish believers rather than as a residual law code.

title: How did the Spirit direct Paul's second journey?
answer: By forbidding Asia and Bithynia, then giving the Macedonian vision.
note: Guidance here is largely negative — closed doors before an open one, which is Luke's realistic picture of discernment.

title: What happened at midnight in the Philippian jail?
answer: Paul and Silas prayed and sang; an earthquake opened the doors and loosed the bands.
note: They do not flee, and it is that refusal, not the earthquake, that converts the jailer.

title: How did Paul adapt his preaching at Athens?
answer: He began from their altar and their poets rather than from Israel's Scriptures.
note: The content is unchanged — creation, judgment, resurrection — but the starting point moves; the sermon models contextualisation without compromise.

title: What was the response to the resurrection at Athens?
answer: Some mocked, some deferred, and certain men clave unto him and believed.
note: Luke records a mixed and modest result at the intellectual centre of the world, without treating it as failure.

title: What did Paul say to the Ephesian elders about false teachers?
answer: That grievous wolves would enter, and from among themselves men would arise speaking perverse things.
note: The threat is named as internal as well as external — the leadership itself is a mission field for error.

title: How did Paul describe his ministry to the Ephesians?
answer: Serving with all humility and tears, teaching publicly and from house to house, keeping back nothing profitable.
note: 'The whole counsel of God' (v.27) is the phrase behind the doctrine of expository preaching through all of Scripture, not favourite parts.

title: What did Agabus prophesy about Paul?
answer: That the Jews would bind the owner of the girdle and deliver him to the Gentiles.
note: Notably, the prophecy is accurate but the community's inference — that Paul should not go — is one Paul rejects; prediction does not automatically dictate direction.

title: How does Paul retell his conversion in Acts?
answer: Three times, each tailored to a different audience.
note: The repetition signals its importance to Luke's argument: the chief persecutor's reversal is the strongest evidence for the resurrection he presents.

title: Why did Paul appeal to Caesar?
answer: To escape a transfer to Jerusalem where an ambush awaited, exercising his citizen's right.
note: Legal process becomes the means of fulfilling Acts 23:11 — 'so must thou bear witness also at Rome.'

title: What promise was Paul given during the shipwreck?
answer: That God had given him all who sailed with him, and none would lose his life.
note: Yet Paul still says 'except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved' (v.31) — the promise does not suspend the means.

title: What does the phrase 'no man forbidding him' accomplish at the end of Acts?
answer: It closes the book on a note of unhindered proclamation despite imprisonment.
note: The final Greek word, akolutos ('unhinderedly'), is Luke's last verdict: chains cannot restrain the word.

title: What is the significance of Acts having no formal conclusion?
answer: The narrative is left open, implying the mission continues in the reader's own time.
note: Often called 'the unfinished book' — Theophilus, and every later reader, is positioned as the next chapter.

title: How does Luke portray the relationship between the church and Rome?
answer: Roman officials repeatedly find no crime in the Christians.
note: Luke builds a legal apologia: Christianity is not seditious, and every competent authority who examines it says so.

title: What role do prayer and fasting play in Acts' major decisions?
answer: They precede the sending of missionaries and the appointing of elders.
note: Luke consistently places corporate discernment before institutional action, never the reverse.

title: How many letters are traditionally attributed to Paul?
answer: Thirteen, from Romans to Philemon (fourteen if Hebrews is counted).
note: Thirteen bear his name, and Hebrews' anonymity led to varying ancient opinions; Origen's remark that only God knows who wrote it remains the honest verdict.

title: What is the theme of Romans, stated in chapter 1?
answer: The gospel is the power of God unto salvation; "the just shall live by faith."
note: Paul's thesis in 1:16-17 links the gospel's power, its universality ('to the Jew first, and also to the Greek') and the revelation of God's righteousness in one sentence.

title: What verdict does Romans 3 give on all humanity?
answer: "All have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God."
note: The catena of Old Testament quotations in 3:10-18 is assembled from Psalms, Proverbs and Isaiah, so the indictment is Israel's own Scripture testifying against Israel.

title: What is propitiation, per Romans 3:25?
answer: Christ set forth as the sacrifice that turns away wrath and satisfies God's justice.

title: What contrast does Romans 5 draw between Adam and Christ?
answer: Through one man's disobedience many were made sinners; through one man's obedience many are made righteous.

title: What are the wages of sin, and the free gift of God?
answer: Death — and eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
note: The contrast is deliberate: wages are earned and owed, a gift is neither — Paul chooses two words that cannot be blended.

title: What is Romans 8's opening assurance?
answer: "There is therefore now no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus."
note: 'No condemnation' answers Romans 7's cry, and 'no separation' closes the chapter — the whole of Romans 8 is bracketed by two impossibilities.

title: From what can nothing separate believers?
answer: The love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

title: What does Romans 10 name as the way of salvation?
answer: Confessing with the mouth Jesus as Lord and believing in the heart that God raised him.
note: Confession with the mouth and belief in the heart are presented as a single act with two aspects, not as two separate conditions.

title: How does faith come, per Romans 10?
answer: By hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
note: 'Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God' grounds the necessity of preaching, and Paul's chain of rhetorical questions in verses 14-15 has shaped missionary theology ever since.

title: What is the "living sacrifice" of Romans 12?
answer: Presenting your bodies to God — reasonable service, with a mind renewed rather than conformed to the world.

title: What was the leading problem in the Corinthian church?
answer: Divisions and party spirit — "I am of Paul; and I of Apollos."

title: What did Paul determine to know among the Corinthians?
answer: Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
note: 'Jesus Christ, and him crucified' is stated against the backdrop of Corinth's appetite for rhetorical brilliance; Paul says he came in weakness and fear precisely to prevent faith resting on eloquence.

title: What foundation can no man lay other than the one laid?
answer: Jesus Christ.

title: What is the body of the believer called in 1 Corinthians?
answer: A temple of the Holy Spirit, bought with a price.
note: 'The temple of the Holy Ghost' is applied first to the congregation (3:16) and then to the individual (6:19) — the corporate sense precedes the personal one.

title: What warning accompanies the Lord's Supper?
answer: Not to eat and drink unworthily, but to examine oneself.

title: What is 1 Corinthians 13 called, and what does it rank highest?
answer: The love chapter; faith, hope and love abide, but the greatest is love.
note: The love described is agape, defined by fifteen verbs rather than by feeling — what love does, not what it feels, is the chapter's method.

title: What does Paul call Christ in 1 Corinthians 15:20?
answer: The firstfruits of them that are asleep — the guarantee of the believers' resurrection.

title: What happens if Christ has not been raised?
answer: Preaching is vain, faith is vain, and believers are yet in their sins.
note: Paul draws seven consequences in 1 Corinthians 15:14-19, ending with 'we are of all men most miserable' — he refuses any fallback position of moral value without historical fact.

title: What does 2 Corinthians say about a believer in Christ?
answer: "If any man is in Christ, he is a new creature: the old things are passed away."

title: What is the ministry of reconciliation?
answer: God reconciling the world to himself in Christ and committing the message to believers as ambassadors.
note: 'God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself' makes reconciliation God's initiative toward us, reversing the pagan assumption that sacrifice moves the deity toward the worshipper.

title: What answer did Paul receive about his thorn in the flesh?
answer: "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my power is made perfect in weakness."

title: What crisis prompted Galatians?
answer: Judaizers insisting Gentile believers be circumcised and keep the Law.
note: Galatians is the only Pauline letter without a thanksgiving section — he moves straight from greeting to astonishment, and the omission is itself a rebuke.

title: What does Galatians 2:20 confess?
answer: "I have been crucified with Christ; and it is no longer I that live, but Christ liveth in me."
note: 'I live; yet not I' holds together the reality of the believer's agency and the priority of Christ's, and the phrase 'who loved me, and gave himself for me' makes the atonement personal without making it private.

title: What was the Law's purpose, per Galatians 3?
answer: A tutor (schoolmaster) to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

title: List the ninefold fruit of the Spirit.
answer: Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, meekness, temperance.
note: Singular "fruit," not "fruits" — one character with nine facets.

title: When did God choose believers, according to Ephesians?
answer: Before the foundation of the world, that they should be holy and without blemish.

title: What is the classic Ephesians statement on salvation?
answer: "By grace have ye been saved through faith... not of works, that no man should glory."
note: 'Not of works, lest any man should boast' is immediately followed by 'created in Christ Jesus unto good works' — Paul excludes works as ground and requires them as purpose in consecutive verses.

title: What did Christ break down between Jew and Gentile?
answer: The middle wall of partition, making both one in himself.

title: Name the pieces of the whole armour of God.
answer: Girdle of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shoes of the gospel of peace, shield of faith, helmet of salvation, sword of the Spirit — with prayer.
note: Every item is drawn from Isaiah's descriptions of God's own armour (Isa 11:5; 59:17); the believer wears what God wears.

title: What is the theme of Philippians?
answer: Joy in Christ regardless of circumstance — written from prison.

title: What does the Philippians 2 "kenosis" hymn teach?
answer: Christ, being in the form of God, emptied himself, took the form of a servant, and was obedient unto death — therefore highly exalted.
note: He laid aside not deity but the independent exercise of divine privilege.

title: What is Paul's summary of life and death in Philippians?
answer: "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain."

title: What does Colossians say about Christ and creation?
answer: He is the image of the invisible God, firstborn of all creation; all things were created through him and unto him.
note: All things were created by him, through him and for him, and 'by him all things consist' — Christ is presented as agent, goal and sustaining principle of the cosmos in a single sentence.

title: What dwells bodily in Christ, per Colossians?
answer: All the fulness of the Godhead.

title: What does 1 Thessalonians 4 teach about the Lord's coming?
answer: The dead in Christ shall rise first, then the living shall be caught up together with them to meet the Lord in the air.

title: What threefold command closes 1 Thessalonians 5?
answer: Rejoice alway; pray without ceasing; in everything give thanks.

title: What qualification lists does 1 Timothy give?
answer: Qualifications for overseers (bishops) and for deacons.

title: What does 1 Timothy 2:5 affirm?
answer: "There is one God, one mediator also between God and men, himself man, Christ Jesus."

title: What does 2 Timothy say about the origin and use of Scripture?
answer: Every scripture is inspired of God ("God-breathed") and profitable for teaching, reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness.
note: 'Theopneustos' means God-breathed rather than merely inspired in the modern sense, and the four uses — doctrine, reproof, correction, instruction — cover both belief and conduct.

title: What was Paul's final testimony in 2 Timothy?
answer: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith."

title: What is the occasion of Philemon?
answer: Paul appeals for Onesimus, a runaway slave, to be received back "no longer as a servant, but... a brother beloved."

title: How does Hebrews open its argument?
answer: God, who spoke in the prophets, has in these last days spoken in his Son — the effulgence of his glory.

title: How does Hebrews define faith?
answer: "The assurance of things hoped for, the proving of things not seen."
note: 'Substance' (hypostasis) and 'evidence' (elenchos) are both concrete, near-legal terms; Hebrews defines faith as a firm reality, not as a feeling of confidence.

title: What does Hebrews call Jesus regarding faith?
answer: The author and perfecter of our faith.

title: What test does James apply to faith?
answer: Faith without works is dead — genuine faith shows itself in action.
note: James asks whether faith can save when it is 'alone' — his target is the person who says he has faith, not faith itself, as the Greek of 2:14 makes clear.

title: What does James say about the tongue?
answer: A small member that boasts great things — a fire, which no man can tame.
note: The images escalate — bit, rudder, fire, poison — and 3:2 concedes that anyone who does not stumble in word is a perfect man, making speech the master test of maturity.

title: What does James call pure religion?
answer: Visiting the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and keeping oneself unspotted from the world.

title: What does 1 Peter call believers corporately?
answer: An elect race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession.

title: What does 2 Peter say about the origin of prophecy?
answer: No prophecy came by the will of man; holy men spake being moved by the Holy Spirit.

title: Why does 2 Peter say the Lord delays his coming?
answer: He is longsuffering, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

title: What twin tests of genuine faith does 1 John apply?
answer: Right belief about Christ come in the flesh, and love of the brethren.

title: What promise does 1 John 1:9 give?
answer: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive and to cleanse from all unrighteousness.
note: God is called 'faithful and just' to forgive, not merely merciful — forgiveness is grounded in his justice being satisfied at the cross, not in overlooking the offence.

title: What twofold definition of God does 1 John give?
answer: God is light, and God is love.

title: What does Jude urge believers to do?
answer: To contend earnestly for the faith once for all delivered unto the saints.

title: What is God's invisible nature known by, per Romans 1?
answer: The things that are made, so that men are without excuse.

title: What threefold 'God gave them up' appears in Romans 1?
answer: To uncleanness, to vile affections, and to a reprobate mind.

title: What is the law written in the hearts of Gentiles?
answer: The work of the law, their conscience also bearing witness.

title: How does Romans 4 show justification is not by works?
answer: Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision, so the promise is by faith to all who believe.

title: What does Romans 6 say about grace and continuing in sin?
answer: 'God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?'

title: What does baptism picture in Romans 6?
answer: Burial with Christ into death, and rising to walk in newness of life.

title: What conflict does Romans 7 describe?
answer: 'The good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.'

title: What does the Spirit do in our infirmities?
answer: He maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.

title: What is the golden chain of Romans 8:29-30?
answer: Foreknew, predestinated, called, justified, glorified.

title: What does Romans 11 say about God's gifts and calling?
answer: They are 'without repentance' — irrevocable.

title: What does Romans 13 teach about governing authorities?
answer: They are ordained of God, ministers for good, to whom tribute and honour are due.

title: What is the fulfilling of the law, per Romans 13?
answer: Love, which worketh no ill to his neighbour.

title: What does Romans 14 say about doubtful things?
answer: 'Whatsoever is not of faith is sin'; let no man put a stumblingblock before his brother.

title: What does 1 Corinthians say the preaching of the cross is?
answer: Foolishness to them that perish, but the power of God to us who are saved.

title: What two things do Jews and Greeks seek, per 1 Corinthians 1?
answer: Jews require a sign, Greeks seek after wisdom; Paul preaches Christ crucified.

title: Who can receive the things of the Spirit of God?
answer: Not the natural man, for they are spiritually discerned.

title: What materials are tested by fire in 1 Corinthians 3?
answer: Gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble.
note: This passage sits at the centre of the Catholic–Protestant debate on purgatory; the text speaks of works tested, with the man himself saved 'so as by fire.'

title: What does 1 Corinthians say about temptation?
answer: God is faithful and will with the temptation make a way to escape.

title: What are the nine gifts listed in 1 Corinthians 12?
answer: Wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, tongues, interpretation.

title: What image describes the church in 1 Corinthians 12?
answer: One body with many members, none able to say to another, 'I have no need of thee.'

title: What order does Paul require for tongues in the assembly?
answer: By two or at most three, in course, and let one interpret; all things decently and in order.

title: What is the gospel Paul defines in 1 Corinthians 15?
answer: Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures, was buried, and rose again the third day.

title: What is the last enemy to be destroyed?
answer: Death.

title: What kind of body is raised, per 1 Corinthians 15?
answer: Sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body; incorruption and immortality put on.

title: What comfort does 2 Corinthians 1 give about affliction?
answer: God comforts us so we may comfort others with the comfort we ourselves received.

title: What does 2 Corinthians say about the treasure and the vessel?
answer: 'We have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God.'

title: What do we walk by, and not by?
answer: 'We walk by faith, not by sight.'

title: What great exchange does 2 Corinthians 5:21 state?
answer: He made him to be sin for us who knew no sin, that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.
note: The double imputation here is the hinge of the Reformation doctrine of justification.

title: What kind of giver does God love?
answer: 'A cheerful giver.'

title: What are the weapons of our warfare?
answer: Not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.

title: What curse does Paul pronounce on another gospel?
answer: 'Let him be accursed' — even were it an angel from heaven.

title: Whom did Paul withstand to the face at Antioch?
answer: Peter (Cephas), because he was to be blamed over table fellowship with Gentiles.

title: What does Galatians say about distinctions in Christ?
answer: 'There is neither Jew nor Greek, bond nor free, male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.'

title: How does Paul describe our adoption cry?
answer: The Spirit of his Son in our hearts, crying, 'Abba, Father.'

title: What law does Galatians 6 say fulfils Christ's?
answer: 'Bear ye one another's burdens.'

title: What principle of sowing does Galatians state?
answer: 'Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.'

title: What is the believer sealed with, per Ephesians 1?
answer: 'That holy Spirit of promise, which is the earnest of our inheritance.'

title: What were we by nature before grace?
answer: 'Dead in trespasses and sins,' children of wrath even as others.

title: On what foundation is the church built?
answer: The apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.

title: What sevenfold unity does Ephesians 4 list?
answer: One body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father.

title: What fivefold ministry gifts does Ephesians 4 name?
answer: Apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers.

title: What does Ephesians say about anger and the sun?
answer: 'Let not the sun go down upon your wrath.'

title: What model does Ephesians 5 give for husbands?
answer: 'Even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it.'

title: Against whom do we wrestle, per Ephesians 6?
answer: 'Not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers.'

title: What confidence does Philippians 1:6 give?
answer: That he who began a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ.

title: What does Philippians say every knee will do?
answer: Bow at the name of Jesus, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
note: Paul takes Isaiah 45:23, spoken by YHWH of himself, and applies it directly to Jesus.

title: What did Paul count all things but loss for?
answer: 'The excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord.'

title: What had Paul learned in whatsoever state he was?
answer: To be content — 'I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.'

title: What are believers told to think on in Philippians 4:8?
answer: Whatsoever things are true, honest, just, pure, lovely, of good report, virtuous and praiseworthy.

title: What is Christ called in Colossians 1:15?
answer: 'The image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.'
note: 'Firstborn' here is rank, not origin: verse 16 says all things were created by him, so he cannot be among created things.

title: What mystery does Colossians reveal?
answer: 'Christ in you, the hope of glory.'

title: What does Colossians say to set our affection on?
answer: Things above, not on things on the earth, since we are risen with Christ.

title: What does Colossians say about doing all things?
answer: 'Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.'

title: What does 1 Thessalonians say about grieving for the dead?
answer: Not to sorrow as others which have no hope, for God will bring them with Jesus.

title: How does the day of the Lord come?
answer: 'As a thief in the night.'

title: What rule of work does 2 Thessalonians give?
answer: 'If any would not work, neither should he eat.'

title: What does 1 Timothy call the love of money?
answer: 'The root of all evil.'

title: What did Paul charge Timothy about his youth?
answer: 'Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers.'

title: What spirit has God not given us?
answer: 'The spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.'

title: How is a workman to handle the word?
answer: 'Rightly dividing the word of truth,' study to shew thyself approved unto God.

title: What does Titus say grace teaches?
answer: To deny ungodliness and worldly lusts, and live soberly, righteously and godly in this present world.

title: What does Hebrews 4 say about the word of God?
answer: It is quick and powerful, sharper than any twoedged sword, a discerner of thoughts and intents.

title: Why can our High Priest be touched with our infirmities?
answer: He was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.

title: What does Hebrews say is appointed unto men?
answer: 'Once to die, but after this the judgment.'

title: What does Hebrews say about forsaking the assembling?
answer: Do not forsake it, as the manner of some is, but exhort one another.

title: What is the 'cloud of witnesses' exhortation?
answer: Lay aside every weight and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and run with patience.

title: Whom does the Lord chasten?
answer: 'Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.'

title: Without what shall no man see the Lord?
answer: Holiness, followed with peace with all men.

title: What is Jesus Christ said to be in Hebrews 13:8?
answer: 'The same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.'

title: What does James say about trials?
answer: Count it all joy; the trying of your faith worketh patience.

title: What must the hearer also be?
answer: 'Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.'

title: What does James say about wisdom lacking?
answer: Ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally and upbraideth not.

title: How does James describe the prayer of a righteous man?
answer: 'The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much,' citing Elias.

title: What does 1 Peter say about our inheritance?
answer: It is incorruptible, undefiled, and fadeth not away, reserved in heaven.

title: What are believers to be ready to give?
answer: 'A reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear.'

title: What covers a multitude of sins, per 1 Peter?
answer: 'Fervent charity among yourselves.'

title: What should believers do with their care?
answer: 'Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.'

title: How does 1 Peter describe the adversary?
answer: 'As a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.'

title: What sevenfold ladder of virtue does 2 Peter give?
answer: To faith add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, charity.

title: What does 2 Peter say a day is with the Lord?
answer: 'One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.'

title: What does 1 John say about claiming sinlessness?
answer: 'If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.'

title: Who is our advocate with the Father?
answer: 'Jesus Christ the righteous,' the propitiation for our sins and for the whole world's.

title: What test does 1 John give for the spirits?
answer: Every spirit that confesseth Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God.

title: What casts out fear?
answer: 'Perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment.'

title: Why were the things of 1 John 5:13 written?
answer: 'That ye may know that ye have eternal life.'
note: John's stated aim is assurance — a settled knowing, not a hopeful guess.

title: What is Paul's usual letter structure?
answer: Greeting, thanksgiving, doctrinal exposition, ethical exhortation, personal greetings.
note: The 'therefore' at the hinge (Rom 12:1; Eph 4:1; Col 3:1) is a structural signal: ethics is always grounded in preceding doctrine, never freestanding.

title: What does Paul mean by 'the righteousness of God' in Romans?
answer: Both God's own covenant faithfulness and the righteous standing he gives to believers.
note: Luther's recovery of the second sense — a righteousness given rather than demanded — was the psychological trigger of the Reformation.

title: What does Romans 2 say about the Gentile who keeps the law?
answer: That circumcision of the heart, in the spirit, is what counts before God.
note: Paul dismantles ethnic presumption before he builds his doctrine of grace — the argument's order is deliberate.

title: How does Paul use Habakkuk 2:4?
answer: 'The just shall live by faith' anchors his thesis statement in Romans 1:17.
note: The same verse appears three times in the New Testament, and each writer stresses a different word — a case study in apostolic exegesis.

title: What is the significance of Romans 3:23-24 being one sentence?
answer: All have sinned and are justified freely by grace, without a break in the clause.
note: The participle 'being justified' hangs directly off 'all have sinned' — universal condemnation and free justification are grammatically fused.

title: What does 'redemption' mean in Paul's vocabulary?
answer: Purchase out of slavery by payment of a price.
note: The metaphor is drawn from the slave market; 'ye are bought with a price' assumes a real transaction with a real cost.

title: What role does baptism play in Romans 6?
answer: It unites the believer to Christ's death and resurrection, breaking sin's dominion.
note: Paul's answer to antinomianism is not stricter rules but a deeper account of union: the believer cannot live in what he died to.

title: What is the 'law of the Spirit of life'?
answer: The liberating principle in Christ that frees from the law of sin and death.
note: Romans 7's frustration is answered not by more effort but by a different power source — the Spirit does what the law could not (8:3).

title: What does Romans 8:28 actually promise?
answer: That all things work together for good to those who love God and are called according to his purpose.
note: Verse 29 defines 'good' as conformity to Christ's image — the promise is about formation, not comfort.

title: What is Paul's anguish in Romans 9?
answer: He could wish himself accursed from Christ for his kinsmen's sake.
note: The doctrine of election in Romans 9 is framed by tears, not triumph — a context often lost in later polemics.

title: What does Romans 11 say about the olive tree?
answer: Gentile branches are grafted in and must not boast against the natural branches.
note: The warning 'if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee' has been ignored across much of church history.

title: What are the marks of genuine love in Romans 12?
answer: Love without dissimulation, abhorring evil, preferring one another, blessing persecutors.
note: Effectively a commentary on the Sermon on the Mount, showing how deeply Paul's ethics are shaped by Jesus' teaching.

title: How does Paul handle disputes over food and days?
answer: By requiring each to be fully persuaded and neither to despise nor judge the other.
note: He classes these as adiaphora — matters indifferent — while treating the manner of disagreement as anything but indifferent.

title: What was the Corinthian party spirit?
answer: Factions claiming Paul, Apollos, Cephas or Christ.
note: Even 'I am of Christ' is listed as a faction — the sectarian spirit can hijack the best slogan.

title: What does Paul say about servants of the church?
answer: Ministers by whom you believed — one plants, one waters, God gives the increase.
note: The deflation is deliberate: the Corinthians are ranking celebrities, and Paul reduces the whole class to gardeners.

title: How does Paul handle the incestuous man?
answer: By requiring the church to remove him, that his spirit may be saved.
note: The stated aim of the severest discipline in the New Testament is restoration; 2 Cor 2:6-8 appears to record its success.

title: What is Paul's argument about lawsuits between believers?
answer: That it is better to be defrauded than to sue a brother before unbelievers.
note: The reputational witness of the church outweighs the individual's right to redress — an argument almost never made today.

title: What is Paul's principle of becoming all things to all men?
answer: Voluntary accommodation in matters indifferent, for the sake of the gospel.
note: Bounded by 1 Cor 9:21 — 'not without law to God' — the flexibility is in method, never in truth or morals.

title: What warning does Paul draw from the wilderness generation?
answer: That they were baptized and ate spiritual food, yet were overthrown; let him that thinketh he standeth take heed.
note: Sacramental participation is no automatic guarantee — a text used heavily in debates on perseverance.

title: What is the 'more excellent way' of 1 Corinthians?
answer: Love, without which tongues, prophecy, knowledge and sacrifice profit nothing.
note: The chapter sits deliberately between two chapters on spiritual gifts — it is corrective, not a wedding reading.

title: What order of resurrection does Paul give?
answer: Christ the firstfruits, afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.
note: 'Firstfruits' implies the rest of the harvest is guaranteed by the same field and season, not merely hoped for.

title: What does Paul call the last enemy, and how is it destroyed?
answer: Death, swallowed up in victory when this mortal puts on immortality.
note: Paul fuses Isa 25:8 and Hos 13:14 into a taunt song — the tone at the doctrine's climax is mockery of death.

title: What is Paul's 'thorn in the flesh' teaching?
answer: That God's strength is perfected in weakness, so he glories in infirmities.
note: The thorn is never identified, which allows every sufferer to find themselves in it; the answer given is grace, not removal.

title: What is the 'letter and spirit' contrast in 2 Corinthians 3?
answer: The letter kills, but the spirit gives life.
note: Not a licence for loose interpretation, but a contrast between the old covenant's written code and the new covenant's inward power.

title: How does Paul describe apostolic ministry in 2 Corinthians?
answer: Troubled but not distressed, perplexed but not in despair, cast down but not destroyed.
note: The catalogue of hardships (2 Cor 11:23-28) is offered as apostolic credentials — Paul boasts in the opposite of what his rivals boast in.

title: What does Galatians say about the Judaizers' motive?
answer: That they desired to make a fair show in the flesh and avoid persecution for the cross.
note: Paul diagnoses legalism as fundamentally a strategy for social safety, not excessive zeal for holiness.

title: What allegory does Paul draw from Hagar and Sarah?
answer: Two covenants — bondage from Sinai and freedom from the Jerusalem above.
note: Paul explicitly labels his own reading 'an allegory,' one of the clearest apostolic warrants for figural interpretation.

title: What is the works of the flesh list in Galatians?
answer: Adultery, idolatry, hatred, variance, wrath, strife, envyings, drunkenness and more.
note: More than half are relational sins of community breakdown, not private vices — a corrective to purely individual holiness.

title: What are the three great blessings of Ephesians 1?
answer: Chosen by the Father, redeemed by the Son, sealed by the Spirit.
note: In Greek verses 3-14 are one enormous sentence, structured in three movements each closing with 'to the praise of his glory.'

title: What is 'the mystery' Paul says was hidden and now revealed?
answer: That Gentiles are fellow heirs and of the same body with Israel.
note: Mystery in Paul means a revealed secret, not an unsolvable puzzle — and its content is chiefly the union of Jew and Gentile.

title: What is the purpose of the ministry gifts in Ephesians 4?
answer: To perfect the saints for the work of the ministry, edifying the body of Christ.
note: The punctuation of this verse is theologically loaded: it makes the saints the ministers and the gifted leaders their equippers.

title: What is the Philippian 'mind of Christ'?
answer: Esteeming others better than oneself, as Christ emptied himself and became obedient to death.
note: The christological hymn is introduced to settle a squabble between two women (Phil 4:2) — the highest theology deployed for the most ordinary conflict.

title: What does Colossians say about philosophy and vain deceit?
answer: To beware of being spoiled by tradition of men and rudiments of the world, not after Christ.
note: The target is a specific syncretism involving angels, asceticism and calendar, not learning as such.

title: What is the Colossian answer to asceticism?
answer: Such rules have a show of wisdom but no value against the indulgence of the flesh.
note: Paul argues that external severity often feeds the very pride it claims to fight — the deepest critique of legalism in his letters.

title: How does 1 Thessalonians describe the church's reputation?
answer: Their faith to God-ward spread abroad so Paul needed to say nothing.
note: They turned 'from idols to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son' — conversion, service and expectation in one sentence.

title: What does 2 Thessalonians say must come before the day of the Lord?
answer: A falling away first, and the man of sin revealed.
note: Paul writes to calm eschatological panic, not stoke it — the pastoral aim is stability, and the 'restrainer' of v.6 remains famously unidentified.

title: What is the pastoral epistles' recurring concern?
answer: Sound doctrine, qualified leaders, and orderly household conduct.
note: The Greek behind 'sound' is hygiainos — healthy doctrine, a medical metaphor casting error as disease rather than mere mistake.

title: What does 1 Timothy say God desires?
answer: That all men be saved and come unto the knowledge of the truth.
note: A key text in the Calvinist–Arminian debate, read as either God's universal desire or his desire for all kinds of people.

title: What does Hebrews mean by Christ being 'better'?
answer: Better than angels, Moses, Aaron, the covenant, the sacrifices and the tabernacle.
note: The comparative 'better' (kreitton) appears thirteen times; the argument is not that Judaism was bad but that it was preliminary.

title: What are the warning passages of Hebrews?
answer: Five solemn warnings against drifting, hardening, falling away, refusing and turning back.
note: Hebrews 6 is among the most contested passages in Scripture, read variously as hypothetical, as describing the unregenerate, or as genuine apostasy.

title: What is the argument of Hebrews 7 about Melchizedek?
answer: That a greater priesthood than Aaron's existed, and Levi paid tithes in Abraham's loins.
note: The argument depends on the silence of Genesis about Melchizedek's genealogy — an early example of arguing from what Scripture does not say.

title: What does Hebrews say about repeated sacrifice?
answer: That a priest standing daily proves the work is unfinished, while Christ sat down.
note: The seated posture is the argument: there were no chairs in the tabernacle, because a priest's work was never done.

title: What is the theme of James in one line?
answer: That genuine faith is visible in conduct, speech, and treatment of the poor.
note: James and Paul use 'justify' differently — Paul of standing before God, James of demonstrated authenticity; both quote Gen 15:6.

title: What does James say about partiality?
answer: That favouring the rich over the poor in the assembly is sin and breaks the royal law.
note: The scene he describes — good seats for the well-dressed — is one of the most concrete pieces of social criticism in the New Testament.

title: What is 1 Peter's central pastoral strategy?
answer: To reframe suffering as participation in Christ's, and believers as strangers and pilgrims.
note: The exile motif governs the letter: Christians are a diaspora people, which shapes both their patience and their distinctness.

title: What does 1 Peter say about submission and witness?
answer: That conduct may win others without a word, and that we honour all men, even the emperor.
note: Written under Nero, the command to honour the king is an extraordinary instance of witness under hostile power.

title: What is the theme of Jude and 2 Peter's overlap?
answer: Both confront false teachers with parallel Old Testament examples of judgment.
note: The close literary relationship is a standard case study in New Testament source criticism, with most holding Jude the earlier.

title: How does 1 John test the claim to know God?
answer: By obedience, love of the brethren, and confession of Christ come in the flesh.
note: John repeatedly writes 'hereby we know' — the letter is structured as a set of diagnostic tests for assurance.

title: What does the word "apocalypse" mean?
answer: Unveiling or revelation — the disclosure of what is hidden.

title: Who wrote Revelation, and from where?
answer: John, exiled on the isle called Patmos for the word of God.
note: Patmos was a Roman penal settlement, and John describes himself as a companion 'in tribulation' — the visions of the throne come to a man under sentence.

title: What blessing opens Revelation?
answer: Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear and keep the words of the prophecy.
note: One of seven beatitudes scattered through the book.

title: What threefold outline does Revelation 1:19 give?
answer: The things seen, the things which are, and the things which shall come to pass hereafter.

title: Name the seven churches of Asia.
answer: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea.
note: The seven form a natural postal circuit around western Asia Minor, so the letters were probably designed to be read in every church, not only the one addressed.

title: Which two churches receive no rebuke?
answer: Smyrna and Philadelphia — the persecuted and the faithful with little strength.

title: What was Ephesus' fault, and Laodicea's?
answer: Ephesus left its first love; Laodicea was lukewarm and self-satisfied.

title: Who alone was worthy to open the sealed book?
answer: The Lion of the tribe of Judah, who appears as a Lamb standing as though slain.
note: John hears "Lion" and sees "Lamb" — the book's central reversal.

title: What are the three series of sevens in Revelation?
answer: Seven seals, seven trumpets, and seven bowls (vials) of wrath.

title: Who are the 144,000?
answer: Those sealed out of every tribe of the children of Israel, twelve thousand from each.
note: Twelve thousand from twelve tribes is a squared and multiplied number signalling completeness; the tribal list is irregular, omitting Dan and splitting Joseph, which most read as symbolic rather than genealogical.

title: Who is the great multitude of Revelation 7?
answer: An innumerable crowd out of every nation, tribe, people and tongue, in white robes before the throne.

title: How do the saints overcome the accuser?
answer: By the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony, and not loving their life unto death.
note: The three means in Revelation 12:11 are objective (the blood), verbal (their testimony) and personal (not loving their lives) — none of them is force.

title: How many beasts appear in Revelation 13, and from where?
answer: Two — one out of the sea, one out of the earth.

title: What is Babylon in Revelation?
answer: The great city symbolising organised worldly and religious rebellion against God, destined to fall.

title: What is the marriage supper of the Lamb?
answer: The consummating feast of Christ and his bride, the Church, made ready in fine linen — the righteous acts of the saints.
note: The bride's linen is explicitly interpreted as 'the righteousness of saints' (19:8), yet it is 'granted' to her — the garment is both given and worn.

title: How is Christ described at his return in Revelation 19?
answer: On a white horse, called Faithful and True, in a vesture dipped in blood, named The Word of God.

title: What is the Great White Throne?
answer: The final judgment of all the dead, out of the books, according to their works.
note: Judgment is 'according to their works' from the books, while deliverance is by the book of life — Revelation holds both criteria in the same scene without reconciling them for the reader.

title: What five things are absent from the new creation?
answer: Death, mourning, crying, pain — and the sea; also no more curse, night, or temple.

title: What is the light of the New Jerusalem?
answer: The glory of God, and the Lamb is the lamp thereof — no sun or moon needed.

title: What are the last recorded words of Scripture's prophecy?
answer: "Amen: come, Lord Jesus" — followed by the closing benediction of grace.

title: How does Christ describe himself in Revelation 1:8?
answer: 'I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending... the Almighty.'

title: What did John see holding the seven stars?
